newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian port warns Italian soldiers to stay away.
newsitem.headline: Albanian port warns Italian soldiers to stay away.

text.p: Albanians angered by the sinking of a refugee boat in a collision with an Italian navy ship told Italian soldiers in a planned multinational security force on Sunday to stay away from the southern port of Vlore.
"I warn Italian soldiers not to come to Vlore, otherwise they will be killed," said Aida, 35, who attended a rally of some 7,000 people in Vlore to mourn the dead.

Albanian politicians and the public expressed outrage at the sinking of the crowded boat, which had left from Vlore and sank after an Italian corvette tried to intercept it in the southern Adriatic on Friday.
"According to our information, 79 people are missing. They are mostly women and children. This is a national tragedy," Foreign Minister Arjan Starova told parliament.

Italy said four bodies had been recovered and 34 survivors picked up. The corvette was enforcing Italy's policy of turning back illegal refugees trying to flee from widespread civil strife in Albania.

Anger was especially strong in Vlore, centre of a month-long revolt against rightist President Sali Berisha and embarkation point for the ill-fated refugees. Many refugees came from Vlore itself and have families there.
"If a ferryboat comes to Vlore from Italy we will take our revenge," Kranar, 27, said at the rally.

In a statement to the crowd, the self-styled Committee of Public Salvation called on Italy to compensate the families of the dead and do everything possible to recover the bodies and send them home for burial.

"We accuse the Italian government of intentionally sinking the Albanian patrol boat and call it an irresponsible killer," it said, adding that an international court should "rule on the matter and punish the guilty."

Diplomats in Tirana said the Italian-led multinational force, expected to arrive in Albania over the next few weeks to protect international relief efforts, might delay sending troops to Vlore because of the hostility there.

"The situation in Vlore was already fragile. This (the sinking) came at a very unfortunate time and has raised passions in the region. It might be better to deploy elsewhere first," one European Union diplomat said.

The 2,500-strong force is being put together after receiving approval from the United Nations on Friday. Among the countries expected to contribute troops or police participate are Italy, France, Greece, Spain and Portugal.
The plan, pushed hard by Italy, is to send the force to Tirana airport and the ports of Vlore and Durres to protect aid supplies. It will also oversee aid convoys throughout the country.

Italy and Greece, Albania's EU neighbours, have expressed deep concern that the crisis sweeping the Balkan country could trigger a massive wave of illegal immigration. More than 13,000 Albanians have fled to Italy this month.
Both countries were flooded by illegal Albanian workers in 1991 and 1992 after a ruthless Stalinist regime collapsed after 45 years in power.
So far Greece has pledged 1,000 troops for the force and France 800. The total strength is expected to be about 5,000, with about half deployed initially and half in reserve.
